# Two accumulators of two limbs into one

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `acc_merge_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A step of an accumulator: the running sum $t \approx s + v$, and the sum of the magnitudes $b$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$t \approx s + v, \qquad b = \mathrm{RN}(a + c).$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $s = s_0 + s_1$, $v = v_0 + v_1$, $t = t_0 + t_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A.merge(B)` | `Accumulator<T, 2>`, `Accumulator<T, 2>` | `void` | a node of the summation tree; the counts added |

`T` is `float` or `double`; `A` and `B` are accumulators, `kairn::Accumulator<T, k>`, header `kairn/accumulator.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` includes. They take no marker: an operation of an accumulator compiles only while its kernels are proved ([The accumulator](accumulator.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $s$ is normalized: $s_0 = \mathrm{RN}(s_0 + s_1)$.
- $v$ is normalized: $v_0 = \mathrm{RN}(v_0 + v_1)$.
- $a \ge 0$.
- $c \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t$ is normalized: $t_0 = \mathrm{RN}(t_0 + t_1)$.
- $\lvert t - (s + v)\rvert \le \frac{3u^2}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert s + v\rvert$.
- $b = \mathrm{RN}(a + c)$: the number of the format nearest to $a + c$, ties to even.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $\frac{3}{2^{106} - 2^{55}} \approx 3.6978 \times 10^{-32}$ | $\frac{3}{2^{48} - 2^{26}} \approx 1.0658 \times 10^{-14}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1.8000000000004p-105`, `0.0` | `0x1.800008p-47f`, `0.0f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1.8000000000004p-105`, `0.0` | `0x1.800008p-47f`, `0.0f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `acc_merge_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/AccKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/AccKernels.v), against `acc_merge_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions acc_merge_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition acc_merge_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (3 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall s0 s1 a v0 v1 c : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec s0 s1 ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  normalized_2 emin prec v0 v1 ->
  fmt emin prec c ->
  0 <= a ->
  0 <= c ->
  let '(t0, t1, b) := acc_merge_2 emin prec tie_even s0 s1 a v0 v1 c in
  fmt emin prec b /\
  normalized_2 emin prec t0 t1 /\
  Rabs ((t0 + t1) - ((s0 + s1) + (v0 + v1))) <= (3 / (1 - (4 * u prec))) * u prec ^ 2 * Rabs ((s0 + s1) + (v0 + v1)) /\
  b = RN emin prec (a + c).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `acc_merge_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** add_2_2 of two running sums, and the sum of the magnitudes (milestone2.md); [JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17) Alg. 6, bound from [MR22](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#mr22). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/acc_merge_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/acc_merge_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md).

```
# acc.merge(other) of Accumulator<T, 2> (milestone2.md, "The accumulator"): the running sums added,
# as add_2_2 (a node of the tree of the summation), and the sums of the magnitudes of the leading
# limbs added, rounded to nearest. The counts are added in the header. Both accumulators are
# objects: nothing comes from the program.

(t0, t1) = add_2_2(s0, s1, v0, v1)
b        = add(a, c)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb` and the supplementary run of commit `8ee5ed9`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#acc_merge_2)).

**These runs judged other claims.** They judged `normalized(t)`; `error(t) form R, c=3/(1-4*u), k=2, t=0`; `rounded(b) nearest of a+c`; the kernel now claims `normalized(t)`; `error(t) form R, c=3/(1-4*u), k=2, t=0`; `rounded(b) nearest`. Their numbers are not about the statement above.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 011 252 | 0 | 0.666667 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 009 452 | 0 | 0.629769 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 3 domains of 3 formats (**a guard failed**) | 482 936 | 0 | 0 (`fp:3:-2:-1`) | no |
| toy formats, every operand, supplementary run: 2 domains of 2 formats | 1 218 961 | 0 | 0 (`fp:3:-3:-1`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
